updates.bio: Program Manager at NOAA's Office for Coastal Management who heads its Ecosystems Program, the office that implements the 30-site National Estuarine Research Reserve System. Works with teams nationwide on program development and technical assistance to improve coastal management. Studied estuaries and the interplay of science and policy; holds bachelor's and master's degrees in marine biology.
updates.current_title: Program Manager, Ecosystems Program (implements the National Estuarine Research Reserve System)
updates.evidence: I am the manager of the Office for Coastal Management's (OCM) Ecosystems Program. We implement the National Estuarine Research Reserve System
updates.notes: NOS career profile (page last updated 09/23/26), written in first person, so the bio uses no pronoun. A career-timeline block (B.S. Atmospheric Science, 2005 data analyst) sits inside an HTML comment on the page and does not match the stated marine biology education; not used. updates.bio: Senior Research Ecologist at Colorado State University's Natural Resource Ecology Laboratory and, per that lab's biography, a U.S. Geological Survey senior scientist. She founded the Loch Vale Watershed long-term monitoring effort in Rocky Mountain National Park and is its principal investigator, and studies how climate change and nitrogen deposition affect mountain ecosystems. She was ESA President in 2014.
updates.research_interests: climate change effects on mountain ecosystems; atmospheric nitrogen deposition and biogeochemistry; reactive nitrogen pollution; ecosystem concepts for managing human-dominated regions; long-term watershed monitoring
updates.current_title: Senior Research Ecologist, Natural Resource Ecology Laboratory
updates.evidence: She is founder and Principal Investigator of the Loch Vale Watershed long-term monitoring and research program in Rocky Mountain National Park

That program grants permits for field studies at reserve sites, provides long-term environmental monitoring data and graduate fellowships, and offers its sites as reference areas for comparative coastal research.

That program serves K-12 groups, teachers, the public and coastal decision-makers through field trips, summer camps, outreach talks, educator workshops and curriculum materials on estuaries.

updates.bio: Manager since 2005 of North Carolina's Coastal Reserve and National Estuarine Research Reserve program, part of the state Division of Coastal Management, overseeing research, education, training and stewardship across its 10 sites. She holds marine biology and marine science degrees, championed NOAA's Davidson Graduate Fellowship, and formerly led the National Estuarine Research Reserve Association as president.
